summary.one_liner: Uptime Kuma is an easy-to-use self-hosted monitoring tool that checks the uptime of websites, servers, and services and sends notifications when they go down.
keywords: watch if my site is down
get alerts when website goes down
summary.what_it_does: Uptime Kuma monitors HTTP(s), TCP, HTTP(s) keyword, HTTP(s) JSON query, WebSocket, ping, DNS record, push, Steam game server, and Docker container targets. It provides a web UI with a ping chart and certificate info for each monitor. It sends notifications through Telegram, Discord, Gotify, Slack, Pushover, email (SMTP), and 90+ other services. Users can create multiple status pages and map them to specific domains. The app also offers multi-language support, proxy support, and 2FA login. The README describes it as running on Docker (Compose or a single docker run command) or directly with Node.js, optionally under PM2.
use_cases: Get alerts when a site goes down
Publish a public status page for services
Check TCP ports or DNS records
Self-host an alternative to Uptime Robot
how_to_run: curl -o compose.yaml <URL from README> && docker compose up -d
git clone <repo URL> && cd uptime-kuma && npm run setup
notable: Wide range of monitor types, including Docker containers, Steam game servers, and push monitors
Notifications to Telegram, Discord, Gotify, Slack, Pushover, SMTP email, and 90+ other services
Multiple status pages that can be mapped to specific domains
Runs via Docker or directly on Node.js on Linux and Windows 10/Server 2012 R2 or higher
Uses WebSocket rather than a REST API for the single-page app
caveats: NFS and similar network file systems are not supported for data storage; map to a local directory or volume
Non-Docker install is not supported on FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, Replit, or Heroku
Non-Docker install requires Node.js 20.4 or newer, Git, and optionally PM2
The README says the author cannot provide support by email; questions go to GitHub Issues or the subreddit
